newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD sees Spain, Portugal deficits at EMU levels.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Spain, Portugal deficits at EMU levels.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development (OECD) indicated on Thursday that the budget deficits in Spain and Portugal were set to fall enough for these countries to qualify for the European single currency.

In its half-yearly Economic Outlook, the OECD said that the budget deficit in Spain would drop from 4.5 percent in 1996 to 3.0 percent in 1997 and 2.6 percent in 1998. For Portugal, the deficit was projected to fall from 4.0 percent in 1996 to 2.9 percent in 1997 and 2.8 percent in 1998.

Under a strict interpretation of the Maastricht terms for economic and monetary convergence on the way to the single European currency, countries have to bring back their budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
